issues.description: File size is extremely large (26,832 tokens). This suggests a God Object anti-pattern where a single class has too many responsibilities.
issues.suggestion: Consider splitting the MiniSearch class into smaller, focused modules. Extract search logic, indexing logic, query execution, and result formatting into separate classes or modules. This will improve testability, maintainability, and code reusability.

issues.description: The addition of 'makeResult' as a private method for extracting result construction logic is good, but indicates that methods in this class are likely too long and doing too much.
issues.suggestion: Review all methods for Single Responsibility Principle violations. If you needed to extract 'makeResult', other methods likely need similar refactoring. Consider extracting more helper methods or creating a separate ResultBuilder class.

issues.description: Filter functions applied at QueryCombination level may have unexpected behavior if not properly validated. Missing validation of filter function parameters could lead to runtime errors.
issues.suggestion: Ensure filter functions are validated before execution: 1) Check if filter is a function, 2) Handle filter function exceptions with try-catch, 3) Add TypeScript type guards to ensure type safety, 4) Document expected filter function signature and behavior.

issues.description: Applying filters at the QueryCombination level after query execution may be inefficient for large result sets. Filters applied post-query mean unnecessary processing.
issues.suggestion: Consider pushing filters down to the query execution level where possible to avoid processing results that will be filtered out. Implement early filtering to reduce memory usage and improve performance for large datasets.

issues.description: Without comprehensive test coverage visible, adding filter support to complex queries introduces regression risk, especially with the modification to 'executeQuerySpec'.
issues.suggestion: Ensure comprehensive test coverage for the new filtering functionality: 1) Unit tests for makeResult method, 2) Integration tests for executeQuerySpec with various filter combinations, 3) Edge case tests (null filters, empty results, complex nested queries), 4) Performance tests for large result sets with filters.

issues.description: The makeResult method extraction suggests result objects are being constructed repeatedly. Without seeing the implementation, there may be opportunities for object pooling or memoization.
issues.suggestion: Review the makeResult implementation for optimization opportunities: 1) Use object pooling for frequently created result objects, 2) Consider memoization if results are deterministic, 3) Avoid creating unnecessary intermediate objects, 4) Use efficient data structures for result storage.

issues.description: Filter functions executing user-provided code could be a security concern if not properly sandboxed, especially if the library is used in a server context.
issues.suggestion: If filter functions accept user input: 1) Document security considerations in the API, 2) Consider implementing timeout mechanisms for filter execution, 3) Warn users about code injection risks if filters are constructed from user input, 4) Provide safe, declarative filter options as an alternative to arbitrary functions.

codeQuality.summary: The TypeScript file is a large implementation (26,832 tokens) with filtering support added for sub-queries. While no obvious security vulnerabilities are detected (no eval, innerHTML, or dangerous patterns), the file size suggests potential maintainability issues. The PR adds a new private method 'makeResult' and modifies 'executeQuerySpec' to apply filters at the QueryCombination level. The code would benefit from modularization and clearer separation of concerns.

recommendations.description: Add comprehensive unit tests for the new makeResult method and integration tests for executeQuerySpec filter application at QueryCombination level. These are core changes that affect all search operations.

Implement proper error handling and validation for filter functions. Add try-catch blocks around filter execution and handle edge cases like null/undefined filters, non-boolean return values, and thrown exceptions.
Add tests for filter edge cases: empty result sets, all results filtered out, null/undefined values, malformed input, and filter performance with large datasets (10K+ documents).

Refactor MiniSearch.ts to eliminate code duplication in filter application logic. Extract match formatting logic from makeResult and implement a filter strategy pattern to reduce duplicated code across multiple branches.

Reorganize the large test file (87,643 characters) into nested describe blocks grouped by feature area (Search, Filtering, Field Boosting, etc.). Extract test setup factories and common filter functions to reduce duplication.
Strengthen TypeScript type safety by adding readonly modifiers to filter functions and search result parameters. Create specific FilterFunction types and ensure immutability in result objects.

Review filter application performance, especially for large result sets. Consider implementing early filtering at the query execution level instead of post-query filtering to avoid processing results that will be filtered out.
Continue the modernization effort started in PR #305 (let to const). Apply additional ES6+ features throughout both files: arrow functions, destructuring, spread operators, and template literals.
Improve test naming to follow 'should [behavior] when [context]' pattern. Extract reusable filter helper functions and create test data builders for more flexible document creation.
Document security considerations for user-provided filter functions. Consider implementing timeout mechanisms for filter execution and warn users about code injection risks.
